segments.content: 2.1.1 Tuen Ma Extension is a railway scheme to improve railway accessibility to Tuen Mun South area. The new extension will serve the community south of Tuen Mun town centre and the new development area of A16. The A16 station is located on the Tuen Mun River waterfront promenade serving the existing catchments on the west bank of the river (i.e. Lung Mun Oasis, Glorious Garden) and east of Hoi Wong Road (i.e. Nerine Cove, Oceania Heights) as well as the future population in the development area of A16.

segments.content: 2.1.2 The Railway Development Strategy 2014 (RDS-2014) published by Transport and Housing Bureau in September 2014 has included TME as one of the recommended railway schemes for implementation. The RDS-2014 stipulated the Governments policy on railway development to unleash the development potential of area along railway lines to facilitate housing and economic developments. The recently released "HK2020+": Towards a Planning Vision and Strategy Transcending 2030" strategic plan that re-affirms that Hong Kong will continues to underscore the compact city through a compact transit-oriented development pattern that is sustainable, efficient and cost-effective.

## 2 INTRODUCTION
## 2.1 Background
2.1.1 Tuen Ma Extension is a railway scheme to improve railway accessibility to Tuen Mun South area. The new extension will serve the community south of Tuen Mun town centre and the new development area of A16. The A16 station is located on the Tuen Mun River waterfront promenade serving the existing catchments on the west bank of the river (i.e. Lung Mun Oasis, Glorious Garden) and east of Hoi Wong Road (i.e. Nerine Cove, Oceania Heights) as well as the future population in the development area of A16.
2.1.2 The Railway Development Strategy 2014 (RDS-2014) published by Transport and Housing Bureau in September 2014 has included TME as one of the recommended railway schemes for implementation. The RDS-2014 stipulated the Governments policy on railway development to unleash the development potential of area along railway lines to facilitate housing and economic developments. The recently released "HK2020+": Towards a Planning Vision and Strategy Transcending 2030" strategic plan that re-affirms that Hong Kong will continues to underscore the compact city through a compact transit-oriented development pattern that is sustainable, efficient and cost-effective.
2.1.3 The 2019 Policy Address published on 16 October 2019 has also addressed that the Hong Kong SAR Government will expedite the implementation of projects proposed in RDS-2014 and invited the MTR Corporation Limited (MTRCL) to commence detailed planning and design for the Tung Chung Line Extension, Tuen Ma Extension and Northern Link in the coming year.
2.1.4 TME is envisaged as approximately 2.4-km extension of Tuen Ma Line by extending the existing viaduct structure from Tuen Mun Station (TUM) overrun to a new elevated terminus along Wu King Road adjacent to Tuen Mun Ferry Pier at Tuen Mun South (TMS).
2.1.5 The proposed new station in Tuen Mun South area will be located adjacent to the Light Rail (LR) stops at Tuen Mun Ferry Pier and Siu Hei Court. It allows interchange between LR and Tuen Ma Line to promote the use of railway as the main mode of public transport and relieve the congestion in LR network.
2.1.6 A new intermediate station, A16 Station, will be located approximately 1.2km south of TUM.
2.2 Purpose of Report
2.2.1 In October 2020, MTRCL appointed AECOM Asia Co. Ltd (hereunder referred AECOM) to carry out the Preliminary Design and Reference Design for the Tuen Ma Extension project.
2.2.2 This Report has been prepared in line with Building Services key deliverable items 2.4B as defined in the Scope of Services document and describes the ongoing development of the Building Services required for the overall "C1501 Consultancy Agreement - Tuen Ma Extension".

## 3.3 Fire Services (FS)
## 3.3.1 Design Objectives
(a) The Fire Services Systems will:
. Minimize loss of life and property in the event of a fire
. Minimize the impact on the operation of the train services in the event of a fire
. Detect the presence of a smoke or fire to give an early warning of a fire condition
. Provide fire protection measures to initiate emergency procedures to limit smoke production, the prevention of fire spread and evacuation
. Provide automatic fire detection and announcements to the staff for the arrangement of safe evacuation of passengers and staff manually in the event of a fire
. Ensure an interface with various systems to provide visual aids such as flashing signage, emergency display messages and AFC gate free wheeling for evacuation
· Alert staff of the outbreak of a fire with minimum delay to enable an early investigation
· Provide automatic fire extinguishing installations to suppress/quench a fire
· Provide manual fire extinguishing installations for firemen/ staff fire fighting purpose
chunks.content:
## 3.3 Fire Services (FS)

## 3.3.1 Design Objectives

(a) The Fire Services Systems will:

. Minimize loss of life and property in the event of a fire

. Minimize the impact on the operation of the train services in the event of a fire

. Detect the presence of a smoke or fire to give an early warning of a fire condition

. Provide fire protection measures to initiate emergency procedures to limit smoke production, the prevention of fire spread and evacuation

. Provide automatic fire detection and announcements to the staff for the arrangement of safe evacuation of passengers and staff manually in the event of a fire

. Ensure an interface with various systems to provide visual aids such as flashing signage, emergency display messages and AFC gate free wheeling for evacuation

· Alert staff of the outbreak of a fire with minimum delay to enable an early investigation

· Provide automatic fire extinguishing installations to suppress/quench a fire

· Provide manual fire extinguishing installations for firemen/ staff fire fighting purpose

segments.content: . The duty fixed fire pump will be automatically initiated by the fire alarm signal with the activation of a break glass unit within the A16 Station. A pressure bleed-off system will be provided to return the minimum amount of water from the fixed fire pump discharge to the FS water tank via a pressure relief valve. This will ensure that the pump running against the closed discharge valve does not get damaged due to churning and overheating.

. The duty fixed fire pump will be automatically initiated by the fire alarm signal with the activation of a break glass unit within the A16 Station. A pressure bleed-off system will be provided to return the minimum amount of water from the fixed fire pump discharge to the FS water tank via a pressure relief valve. This will ensure that the pump running against the closed discharge valve does not get damaged due to churning and overheating.
· Intermediate booster pumps will be provided to maintain sufficient pressure and flow in accordance with Section 5.14 Clause (e)(1) of the Codes of Practice for Minimum Fire Service Installations and Equipment and Inspection, Testing and Maintenance of Installations and Equipment.
. The capacity of the intermediate booster pump shall be capable of providing for any six hydrant outlets, each with a flow of 450l/min at running pressure of not less than 350kPa, operating simultaneously with an aggregate flow of not less than 2700/min aggregate flow. Suitable Start/Stop Push Buttons together with pump running indicator lights and alarm buzzers shall be provided adjacent to Fire Services Inlets to enable Fire Services personnel exercise control of intermediate booster pumps.
. Sufficient fire hydrants and hose reels shall be provided to ensure that the FH/ HR covered areas, which are stipulated in Table 3.15, can be reached by a length of not more than 30m of fire services hose or hose reel tubing.
. Fire services inlets will be provided and positioned adjacent to both the "Designated Emergency Entrance (DEE)" and "Supplementary Emergency Entrance (SEE)" for Station.
. The fire hydrant and hose reel system from the Station will provide sufficient pressure and flow delivery rate to serve the trackside fire hydrants.
(c) The street fire hydrant system will be designed in accordance with the following criteria:
. For the A16 Station, street fire hydrants fed from the town mains / other water sources accepted by FSD and WSD will be installed near the Designated Emergency Entrance and Supplementary Emergency Entrance.
(d) The sprinkler system shall be designed in accordance with the following criteria:
· The design hazard of the sprinkler system for Station and General Areas of the A16 and for Stabling Siding Areas will be to Ordinary Hazard Group 3 (OH3) and High Hazard Process Group 2 (HHP2) respectively.
. The capacity of the sprinkler tank will be provided based on the sprinkler installations demand condition required at Stabling Siding Area, which is considered as the most demanding system on the required water storage capacity, in accordance with the LPC Rules for Automatic Sprinkler Installations incorporating BS EN 12845. Effective water volume of sprinkler tank will be sufficient to satisfy with the minimum water volume for pre-calculated High Hazard Process Group system as shown in Table 10 of BS EN 1284. Since the provision of a direct telephone line linking to Fire Services Communication Centre for the transmission of sprinkler fire alarms will be made, the capacity of the sprinkler water tank can be reduced to 2/3 of its full capacity.
. The design of the sprinkler pumps for OH3 will be based on the Clause 10.7 - Performance characteristics of BS EN 12845. The design of the sprinkler pumps for High Hazard will be based on Table 7 of BS EN 12845 and its performance characteristic will be further fine tuned to be in line with the fully hydraulic calculation.
. The design of the sprinkler pipework will be in accordance with Tables 30 to 35 of BS EN 12845.
. Sprinkler inlets will be provided and positioned adjacent to the "Designated Emergency Entrance (DEE) and Supplementary Emergency Entrance (SEE)" for the Station respectively.

System Parameter
D. Irrigation Water Supply System
1. Supply Flow Rate
i. Irrigation Point 0.2 L/sec per point
2. Supply Pressure
i. Maximum Static Pressure 6 bar
ii. Design Outlet Pressure 1.5 to 6 bar (Pressure reducing valve to be installed if outlet pressure exceeds 6 bar)
3. Water Tank Capacity
i. Storage Requirement Refer to Table 3.19 Rainwater Harvesting System Design Parameters
4. Sizing of Pump and Pressure Vessel
i. Pump Flow Min. 1.1 times of design supply flowrate
E. Air-Conditioning Water Supply System
1. Supply Flow Rate
i. A/C Make-Up (Based on "Code of Practice for Fresh Water Cooling Towers Part 3: Water Treatment Methods 2016 Edition", published by EMSD) Water circulation rate for condensing circuit (l/sec) = Cooling Tower Capacity (TR) x 0.189
Evaporation rate (l/sec) = 0.008 x Water circulation rate for condensing circuit
Drift rate (l/sec) = 0.00005 x Evaporation rate
Concentration rate= 7
Bleed off rate (l/sec) = 0.9/ (concentration rate- 1)
Average bleed-off rate (l/sec) = Bleed-off rate x Circulation rate/ 100
Make-up water (l/sec) = Evaporation rate + Drift rate+ Average bleed-off rate (assumed operating load factor= 1)
2. Supply Pressure
i. Maximum Static Pressure 6 bar
ii. Design Outlet Pressure 1 bar to 6 bar
3. Water Tank Capacity

segments.content:
System Parameter
A. Storm Water Disposal System
1. Rainfall Design Return Period 1 in 200 years (Section 4.9.3.1 in NW&MARWDSM)
2. Design Average Time of Concentration 5 minutes
3. Safety Factor due to Climate Change Impact Design rainfall increase of 13.8%
(Section 6.8 in HKSWDM)
4. Design Rainfall Intensity (for instantaneous flow) (to be applied for gravity drain and sizing of storm water sump pit effective volume.) 365mm/ hr
5. Design Rainfall Intensity – Extreme intensity for durations not exceeding 240 minutes (for sizing of emergency storage volume for storm water sump pit only.) (Table 2 in DSD Stormwater Manual) 90mm/ hr
6. Formula for Calculating Rainwater Flow Rate Rational method
Flow rate Q (l/sec) = Coefficient of surface C (assumed = 1) x Rainfall intensity (mm/ hr) x Catchment area (A)/ 3600
7. Sizing of Stormwater Sump Pit
i. Effective Volume Assumed not less than 5 minutes of instantaneous rainwater flow but minimum 2m3 to keep min. 150mm water depth for pump operation
i.e. Effective volume (m3) = 5 min. x 365mm/hr x area (m2)
Pump continuous operation not less than 5 minutes
ii. Emergency Storage 10 minutes of maximum rainfall inflow (extreme condition)
i.e. Storage (m3) = 10 mins. x maximum rainfall at 1 in 200yr x area (m2)

The table also details the sizing of a stormwater sump pit, including effective volume and emergency storage considerations.

segments.content:
System Parameter
8. Sizing of Stormwater Sump Pump
i. Pump Flow Min. 1.1 x design inflow but min. 5 l/sec per pump
ii. No. of Pumps 100% capacity standby (2 duty + 1 standby; each 100% capacity; Assumed 2 duty pumps failure)
iii. No. of Cycles Not more than 4 no. per hour
B. Waste Water Disposal System
1. Discharge Flow
i. Normal Discharge Flow to Floor Drain/ Channel 0.3 l/sec (1 no. cleansing point)
ii. Fire Discharge Flow to Floor Drain/ Channel
(Applicable to A16 Station and Trackside)		 22.5 l/sec (3 no. fire hydrants)
iii. Concession Sink (Discharge Units (DU) as per Table 5, Pg 112 in PESD Guide, published by IOP) 1.3 DU (l/sec)
2. Sizing of Waste Water Sump Pit
i. Effective Volume To cater for the normal inflows but not less 5 minutes of fire hydrant test flow and 1hr. of seepage rate

i.e. Effective volume (m3) = {5 min. x 22.5l/sec} + {1hr. of seepage flow} (if the sump pit also for collection of trackside seepage water) = 6.75m3 + Seepage flow;

However, it shall be sufficient for pump continuous operation not less than 5minutes and not more than 4 on/ off cycles per hour
ii. Emergency Storage To cater for the emergency inflows:

i.e. Emergency storage (m3) = assumed 4 hrs of half cleansing water flow due to failure/not closed (0.15l/sec) (i.e. tunnel sump/Station cleansing point) + 4 hrs trackside washdown (i.e. the washing water flow for the longest served tunnel at 25m3/km/ hr but not more than 25m3) * 4 hrs seepage

* Since the water tank for tunnel washing is not more than 25m3, the water consumption for each time of tunnel washing is assumed not exceeding 25m3.
iii. Diversity Where a waste water sump pit has been designed for collecting both Station and trackside waste water in the event of a "SINGLE FIRE" and "SINGLE TRACK WASHDOWN" occurring simultaneously has been considered. Therefore, the max. flow from operation of 3 no. fire hydrants plus washdown in the longest tunnel will be considered in the calculations.

System Parameter
A. Storm Water Disposal System
1. Rainfall Design Return Period 1 in 200 years (Section 4.9.3.1 in NW&MARWDSM)
2. Design Average Time of Concentration 5 minutes
3. Safety Factor due to Climate Change Impact Design rainfall increase of 13.8%
(Section 6.8 in HKSWDM)
4. Design Rainfall Intensity (for instantaneous flow) (to be applied for gravity drain and sizing of storm water sump pit effective volume.) 365mm/ hr
5. Design Rainfall Intensity – Extreme intensity for durations not exceeding 240 minutes (for sizing of emergency storage volume for storm water sump pit only.) (Table 2 in DSD Stormwater Manual) 90mm/ hr
6. Formula for Calculating Rainwater Flow Rate Rational method
Flow rate Q (l/sec) = Coefficient of surface C (assumed = 1) x Rainfall intensity (mm/ hr) x Catchment area (A)/ 3600
7. Sizing of Stormwater Sump Pit
i. Effective Volume Assumed not less than 5 minutes of instantaneous rainwater flow but minimum 2m3 to keep min. 150mm water depth for pump operation
i.e. Effective volume (m3) = 5 min. x 365mm/hr x area (m2)
Pump continuous operation not less than 5 minutes
ii. Emergency Storage 10 minutes of maximum rainfall inflow (extreme condition)
i.e. Storage (m3) = 10 mins. x maximum rainfall at 1 in 200yr x area (m2)

Therefore, the max. flow from operation of 3 no. fire hydrants plus washdown in the longest tunnel will be considered in the calculations.

## 3.5 Electrical Services (ES)
## 3.5.1
## Design Objectives
## (a)
The key objectives of the electrical system design are to:
. To ensure a sufficient and high security electrical power supply for the A16 Station and MTR Systemwide E&M systems
. To provide adequate illumination within the Station premises and along the evacuation path for the passengers and staff during the normal operation period and in the event of an emergency condition
· To achieve an energy efficient electrical design
. To maximize the reliability and maintainability of the system
. To ensure a high standard of quality and safety for installation, operation and maintenance

By concerning the light load condition during the night-time, one fresh water-cooled chiller is proposed to operate at night-time. Therefore, two (2) number fresh water cooled chillers each rated at 2,124kW (604 RT) cooling capacity and one (1) number fresh water cooled chiller rated at 1,016kW (289 RT) are proposed to meet the overall cooling requirements for both day-time and night-time operations. Therefore, infiltration is considered not likely to occur during normal operation and hence, it can be disregarded in the cooling load simulation.

## 5.2 11kV Power Supply Network Summary

5.2.1 The 11kV power supply to A16 Station will be fed from CLP. The HV plant and associated cabling works will be supplied and installed by CLP. The design of the Transformer Rooms will comply with CLP Code of Practice No. 101.

5.2.2 In accordance with FSD requirements, transformers fed from two different power supply sources will not be installed within the same Transformer Room.

5.2.3 In order to avoid a blackout caused by the failure of the 11kV power source, a dual electrical power supply system arrangement will be provided. A pair of transformers located in separate transformer rooms will be fed from a different CLP 11kV power source and will be strategically paired together for providing a dual power source to the LV Switch Board.

5.2.5 One of the transformers in each pair will be directly fed by the HV Switch Board installed in the same transformer room. The other transformer in each pair will be cross fed by the HV switch board installed

at the other end of the Station. For this cross-feed arrangement, two (2) out of the four (4) transformer rooms will be equipped with HV switch board.

5.2.6 The power supply source for the south end HV switch board will be fed from CLP 11kV network from one of the nearby primary substation (exact substation name to be advised by CLP) and the north end HV switch board will be fed from alternative CLP 11kV network from another nearby primary substation (exact substation name to be advised by CLP).

5.2.7 The cross-feed 11kV cables between the transformer rooms at both ends of the Station are required to be routed from ground level EVA within A16 Station boundary to the transformer room at the other end by CLP. Exact routing and provisions to be developed and agreed with MTR Systemwide E&M and CLP in detailed design stage.
